clauses.reason: Changes the paragraph 3 report date to 1951-03-01. A report deadline is not an end; the amendment lapsed when the Commission it governed ceased to exist at the end of 1951-05-31 under paragraph 8 as rewritten by EO 10236 (signed 1951-04-26). The cited ACT span ends at the opening quotation mark; the operative sentence 'The Commission shall cease to exist at the end of May 31, 1951' follows at the next characters of the same held text and is read in ACTOR_TEXT:EO:10236. Effective date confirmed in that acting text.

Replaced on 1951-04-26: EO 10236 states that paragraph 8 of EO 10129 'as amended by paragraph 2 of Executive Order No. 10192 ... be, and it is hereby, further amended to read as follows', removing the 'Sixty days' wording; no delayed effective date. Effective date confirmed in the acting text.

research_rationale:
EO 10192 (December 15, 1950, 15 FR 9029) was read in the held official Federal Register extract (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_10192.txt, 19,424 chars). The order is only the two numbered amendments at about chars 15,127-15,308; the rest of the extract is neighbouring Federal Register material including EO 10193. It amends EO 10129 of June 3, 1950 (President's Commission on Migratory Labor, held): para 1 changes the paragraph 3 report date from 'December 15, 1950' to 'March 1, 1951'; para 2 changes 'Thirty days' to 'Sixty days' in paragraph 8 (EO 10129 para 8 as issued: 'Thirty days after rendition of its report to the President, the Commission shall cease to exist unless otherwise determined by further Executive Order'). The first end is EO 10236 (signed 1951-04-26, 16 FR 3607; held official text): 'paragraph 8 ... as amended by paragraph 2 of Executive Order No. 10192 ... be, and it is hereby, further amended to read as follows: "8. The Commission shall cease to exist at the end of May 31, 1951."' Clause 2 (the 'Sixty days' wording) was replaced on 1951-04-26; clause 1 (the changed report date) was spent when the Commission ceased to exist at the end of 1951-05-31, which is also the whole-order end. A report deadline is not an end and the actual report date is not held, so I treated the amendment of a deadline as ending with the body whose report it governed; the independent reviewer should test that choice. The machine searches (usc 0 hits, ecfr 0 hits, OFR catalog 1 hit) carry no coverage warning; the single catalog hit points at EO 10263 only because of a mis-attributed date and is resolved above.

The two clauses therefore have different first ends and the whole-order end is the later date."}

savings.reason: Neither EO 10192 nor EO 10236 contains a saving, transfer or transitional clause; EO 10236 simply provides that the Commission 'shall cease to exist at the end of May 31, 1951'. The Commission's report and expenditures are accrued past acts, not continuing commands.
